# Lab notebook {.unnumbered}

## 2026-09-09 — Program start: from the audit's agenda to preregistered experiments {#sec-nb-start}

**Setting.** The companion review of the ISLA record
(`research/cross_dataset_generalization/`, untracked; rendered report at its `_book/index.html`)
audited the repository, thirty-one primary papers and five analytic
controls, and concluded that the record does not establish a cross-dataset
accuracy advantage for ISLA; with the freestream input matched, GeoTransolver
and Transolver are more accurate at both completed HiLiftAeroML rungs, and on
the DrivAerML → SHIFT-SUV fastback transfer ISLA's source-only error is 0.99
against GeoTransolver's 0.59, both falling to 0.11–0.13 when the estate family
joins training. The review proposed four directions (rich computational
support with independent queries; topology- and conditioning-aware boundary
responses; local flux responses with numerical global coupling; transferred
correction spaces), a physical-input prerequisite, and a nonlinear extension.

**Decision.** This program runs in a worktree parallel to the main ISLA
session (which owns the program book and its cluster lanes) and keeps in
sync with it at milestones. Order of work, as the review recommended:
controls first (C1 pressure-offset versus spatial error, eval-only on saved
predictions; C2 source-only normalization audit; C3 a paired
physical-condition control with exact labels), then in parallel the
computational-support study (D1, which needs training lanes and therefore
node budget from the main program) and the three nonlearned gates (D2
boundary-response rank and basis transfer on 2D Laplace; D3 local-response
composition on 2D diffusion ports; D4 solver correction-space transfer on 2D
finite-element systems), each run by a separate agent in its own worktree
with a preregistration written before its first run. A literature chapter
(L) asks what classical solvers do that surrogates do not.

**Heilmeier answers, compressed.** We want field and force predictions on
geometries and families outside the training distribution without a new
labeled dataset. Today's surrogates fit their family and fail outside it,
and the largest reported advantages in this program turned out to be
protocol artifacts. The new element is not an architecture but a set of
gates: each proposed mechanism has a cheap nonlearned test that can reject
it before training. If it works, the payoff is a surrogate whose failure
modes are understood and whose accuracy is stated with its cost. The risks
are that no mechanism passes its gate (a useful negative), or that a passing
gate does not carry to turbulent 3D data. Cost: CPU studies today; one
four-lane training study when budget allows.

## 2026-09-09 — Preregistered: C1, pressure-offset versus spatial error on the fastback transfer {#sec-nb-c1-prereg}

**Setting.** DrivAerML (static wheels, fixed freestream, OpenFOAM hybrid
RANS–LES) and SHIFT-SUV (rolling floor, rotating wheels, a different
freestream speed and a different detached-eddy formulation) are different
label-generating conventions on smooth single-body car families. Pressure is
nondimensionalized by each dataset's own metadata (q_∞) and not shifted, so
a difference in the two datasets' pressure reference would appear in a
zero-shot prediction as a per-case constant, and a constant is exactly what
makes a relative L2 error approach 1.0 when the predicted field is otherwise
sensible. ISLA's source-only fastback error is 0.99; GeoTransolver's 0.59.

**Instrument (eval-only).** From the saved zero-shot predictions
(`smoke_fastback/{mt2_v3c,gt_fixed,mt2_multi,gt_multi}_seed{42,43,44}`, 99
fastback cases) and the in-family DrivAerML evaluations of the same
checkpoints, with cell areas recomputed from the saved triangles and cell
normals from the saved mesh: per case and arm (seed-mean predictions), the
area-weighted mean error (the offset), the centered remainder, the share of
area-weighted squared error carried by the offset, the relative L2 error of
the full and of the offset-removed error against the centered true field,
the surface closedness |Σ a n| / Σ a, and the relative error of the
integrated pressure force with and without the offset. Script:
`studies/controls/pressure_offset_diagnostic.py`.

**Bars, in readout units.** For the two source-only fastback arms:
*offset-dominated* if the constant carries ≥ 50% of the area-weighted
squared error (median over cases) and the offset-removed relative L2 is at
most 0.6 of the full one; *spatial* if the constant carries ≤ 20%; between,
mixed. The in-family arms must show an offset share ≤ 10%, or the instrument
is not measuring a transfer effect. Force: on surfaces with closedness
≤ 0.05 the force error with and without the offset must agree within the
offset's share, or the normals are inconsistent and the force reading is
withdrawn.

**What each outcome changes.** Offset-dominated: the historical transfer
gap is a label-convention question before it is an architecture question;
C3 (paired physical conditions) becomes the next control, and any transfer
claim must state the pressure reference. Spatial: the gap is a genuine field
error; the offset hypothesis is closed and D1/D2 proceed on their own
merits. Either way the readout is descriptive: target labels are used only
to diagnose, never to correct predictions.

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict: C1 spatial — the zero-shot fastback error is a field error, not a pressure-reference offset (offset share 1.5–2.6% for ISLA, 3.0–3.2% for GeoTransolver) {#sec-nb-c1-verdict}

**Readout** (@sec-nb-c1-prereg; `studies/controls/pressure_offset_2026-09-09.json`;
99 fastback cases, 48 DrivAerML validation cars; seed-mean predictions;
the GeoTransolver source-only and in-family arms use seeds 45 and 46 because
the seed 42–44 predictions of the historical reduction are no longer on
disk, the configuration being identical). Relative errors are on gauge
pressure about the area-weighted case mean, so their scale differs from the
program book's standardized metric; ratios between arms agree with it.

| arm | seeds | rel. L2 (full error) | rel. L2 (offset removed) | offset share of area-weighted squared error | offset ÷ true RMS | force rel. error | force rel. error, offset removed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ISLA, DrivAerML only → fastback | 3 | 1.015 | 1.019 | 1.5% | +0.135 | 1.63 | 1.64 |
| GeoTransolver, DrivAerML only → fastback | 2 | 0.786 | 0.785 | 3.0% | +0.134 | 1.39 | 1.39 |
| ISLA, + estate → fastback | 3 | 0.121 | 0.121 | 0.8% | -0.014 | 0.28 | 0.28 |
| GeoTransolver, + estate → fastback | 3 | 0.101 | 0.101 | 0.2% | -0.004 | 0.20 | 0.20 |
| ISLA, DrivAerML in-family | 3 | 0.093 | 0.093 | 0.4% | +0.000 | 0.04 | 0.04 |
| GeoTransolver, DrivAerML in-family | 2 | 0.085 | 0.085 | 0.2% | -0.000 | 0.04 | 0.04 |

: Surface closedness |Σ a n| / Σ a is 0.024 on the fastback meshes and 0.022
on DrivAerML, so the pressure-force integral is well defined and a constant
offset cannot move it by more than 2.4% of its magnitude; the force columns
agree to that accuracy.

**Verdict: spatial, for both architectures.** The constant carries 1.5%
(ISLA) and 3.0% (GeoTransolver) of the source-only squared error by the
median over cases (2.6% and 3.2% by the mean), far below the 20% floor of the
"spatial" band; removing it changes the relative error by under 1%. The in-family arms pass the instrument check (offset share
under 1%). The offsets that do exist are small and of the same sign for
both models (+0.14 of the true field's RMS), which is consistent with a
modest difference of pressure reference between the datasets but explains
none of the gap. The transfer failure is a spatial field error, and it is
also a force error: 1.6x (ISLA) and 1.4x (GeoTransolver) of the true force
magnitude against 0.04 in-family, falling to 0.28 and 0.20 when the estate
family joins training.

**What it changes.** The pressure-reference hypothesis is closed. The
compound physical-condition mismatch between the datasets (ground and wheel
motion, freestream speed, solver formulation) remains the leading
explanation that is not about architecture, and C3 tests its logic on an
exactly specified problem. Any transfer claim in this program states the
force error alongside the field error, since a field error of 0.9 is a force
error above 100%.

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict: D4 stops — a free geometric coarse grid beats a frozen source-fitted correction space on every held-out elliptic system {#sec-nb-d4-verdict}

The solver-space probe (`studies/solver_spaces/`, preregistered in its
`PREREG.md` before the run, 47 s on one CPU) compared a frozen proper
orthogonal decomposition of smoother-resistant source errors against
equal-dimension classical coarse spaces on 2D finite-element diffusion
systems with holes, under within-family, topology and coefficient shifts.
The frozen space left 0.75–0.96 of the slow-mode error where the geometric
coarse grid left 0.47–0.73 (ratios 0.62–0.76 against bars of 2.0 and 1.5),
and complete solves with it cost 19–72% *more* work than with the classical
space; the per-target oracle decomposition lost to the grid as well. The
mechanism is that solution snapshots span the right-hand sides seen at the
source geometries, not the operator's slow subspace, which for an elliptic
operator under a point smoother is generic smoothness and comes free. The
convection–diffusion variant was uninformative at mesh Péclet 0.5 and is
recorded as not measured. Chapter @sec-solver-spaces has the tables; the
direction's only remaining homes are operator classes where classical
coarse spaces fail, and learned smoothers or prolongations on a classical
hierarchy, both behind prerequisite gates (@sec-classical-solvers).

## 2026-09-09 — C2, source-only normalization: audited from the configurations, one item flagged {#sec-nb-c2-verdict}

Both transfer dataset configurations (`drivaer_ml_surface.yaml`,
`shift_suv_fastback_surface.yaml`) nondimensionalize pressure and wall shear
by each case's own metadata (dynamic pressure) with no shift, and normalize
wall shear by a declared per-dataset constant (standard deviation 0.00313
for DrivAerML, 0.00183 for SHIFT-SUV; zero mean). Inference denormalizes
predictions with the statistics saved at training time (source-side), and
the relative L2 metric is invariant to a common scale, so the differing wall
shear constants do not bias the reported relative errors; they would bias
any absolute or mixed-field loss. Pressure carries no normalization
constant beyond the physical nondimensionalization, so the C1 result is not
a normalization artifact either. Flagged: the wall-shear constant is
target-side in the target configuration (a statistic of SHIFT-SUV chosen
when its config was written); for a zero-shot protocol the target
configuration should carry the source's constant, which changes nothing
for relative metrics and is recorded here as a protocol rule. Verdict:
normalizations are source-only in effect for the reported metrics; one
declared-constant hygiene item.

## 2026-09-09 — Verdict: D3 not worth a learner as proposed — smooth-mode local errors are amplified 4–30x by the interface solve and grids grow superlinearly; the surviving form is a hybrid with exact low modes {#sec-nb-d3-verdict}

The composition gate (`studies/composition/`, preregistered in its
`PREREG.md`, 1,064 s on one CPU) assembled 2D finite-element diffusion
components with identical straight ports into chains and grids of 2–16
components and perturbed every local response by a relative Frobenius error
ε. Exact composition is exact (composition law 2 × 10⁻¹⁶, interface solve
5 × 10⁻¹⁵). At ε = 10⁻² the median global energy error is 1.7% for two
components, 7% for chains of eight, 33% for grids of eight and 34% for grids
of sixteen (a 6.2x growth from four to sixteen, faster than linear), missing
the 5% bar; errors concentrated on rough port modes are damped 20–100x while
errors on smooth modes are amplified 4–30x and set the global error, since
the smooth small-eigenvalue part of a response carries the load (truncating
a response below 63 of 64 modes fails catastrophically). Transfer-optimal
port modes transfer to new shapes but need 13–15 of 15 modes for 1%;
proper-orthogonal modes are shape-specific; at rank 4 both leave 16–27%
error, missing the reduction bar. The interface solve is cheaper than the
monolithic solve only up to four components, and a partition-of-unity coarse
space does not help the iteration count. The narrow-channel family did not
place a barrier at a port, so the near-field claim is untested by this
instrument. Verdict against the bars: not worth a learner as proposed. What
survives is a hybrid solver (exact smooth low-mode response, learned rough
remainder), with a split-response test and a port-adjacent barrier family as
its next nonlearned gates, not launched here. Chapter @sec-composition has
the tables; figures `studies/composition/fig_*.png`.

## 2026-09-09 — D1 launched: six lanes for computational support with a depth-matched passive readout {#sec-nb-d1-launch}

**What was built** (merged from the D1 track, commit 834bd779e on this
branch). `ISLA(support_tokens=True, query_independent=True,
n_query_scalars=1, query_mass="source_total", n_decoder_layers=K)`: the
forward takes `support_points / support_normals / support_scalars`, which
join the encoder as interacting tokens with the same invariant seeds, a
token-type offset and a learned total mass equal to a learned fraction of
the total source measure; requested `query_points / query_normals /
query_scalars` are decoded passively through K read blocks that see the
final slice states, the anchors and a normalized log-space kernel readout of
all encoder tokens. Ten contract tests pass (exact query independence with
the support fixed, at 1e-12, alone or with 500 foreign companions; SE(3)
covariance; drive degree one; measure-scale and source-refinement
invariance; gauge scale equivariance; geo_checkpoint exactness; every
parameter receives gradients); the existing ISLA suites (63) pass. Recipe:
a `SplitInteriorSupport` transform moves the first `n_support` interior
points of the reader's deterministic per-case sample into a
`boundaries.support` mesh carrying the signed distance and its gradient;
dataset `drivaer_ml_volume_support.yaml` (10,000 vehicle cells by
`boundary_subsample: cells`, 10,000 interior points split 5,000 support +
5,000 queries); model `isla_volume_support.yaml`.

**Lanes** (jobs 691276–691281, names v0sup-0..5, launcher
v0/v0_support_aga.sbatch, code snapshot `code_support`, recipe copy
`recipe_support` so the program's frozen recipe is untouched; frozen V0
protocol, unit-direction drive, 500 epochs, lr 1e-3, bf16, seeds 42/43):
SUPPORT-12 (`v0_isla_support12_seed{42,43}`), PASSIVE-12
(`v0_isla_passive12_seed{42,43}`: no support tokens, 12 read blocks with the
SDF scalar) and SUPPORT-4 (`v0_isla_support4_seed{42,43}`). Node budget
confirmed by the main session (25 → 31 of 32 program nodes). Two cluster
conventions were reconciled before submission and are recorded here: the
frozen recipe's model configs carry `# @package _global_` (added to the
repository yaml too) and address surface tokens as
`boundaries.vehicle.cell_normals` / `cell_areas`, so the cluster copy of the
model yaml uses those keys while the repository yaml keeps the nested
`cell_data.*` keys of the upstream-merged recipe; model overrides are
`model.<kwarg>`.

**References and bars** (PREREG.md, written before launch). The support
arms read 10,000 vehicle cells, so their primary reference is the QT+SDF arm
at 10,000 cells (0.0572 / 0.0848 / 0.1187), with the ~365-cell arm
(0.0567 / 0.0853 / 0.1215) reported alongside since V0-SURF10K showed the two
differ by under 3%. Supported if SUPPORT-12 is within 3% of the reference on
all three fields (≤ 0.0584 / 0.0879 / 0.1251 against the 365-cell numbers as
preregistered; ≤ 0.0589 / 0.0873 / 0.1223 against the 10k-cell numbers,
both reported) and the sentinel error is independent of the companion count
within the bf16 floor measured on the legacy passive checkpoint; falsified
if pressure ≥ 0.0624; between, the SUPPORT-4 and PASSIVE-12 arms decompose
depth against interaction.

## 2026-09-09 — Finding while building D1: the legacy passive kernel readout clamps the kernel mass, so far-from-surface queries scale with the absolute source weights {#sec-nb-passive-clamp}

In `physicsnemo/experimental/nn/isla/model.py`, the passive decoder's local
token readout `_kernel_readout(q_r, src_r, src_h, src_w, rho, eps)` (called
from `_ReadBlock.forward` when `src_h` is given, with
`rho = local_readout_rho`, default 0.02 in gauge-normalized coordinates)
computes `k = exp(-d²/ρ²) · w` and divides by `mass = k.sum(-1).clamp_min(eps)`.
For a query farther than a few ρ from every source point the true mass is
below `eps = 1e-12`, the clamp replaces it, and the readout becomes
`Σ k h / eps`, which scales with the absolute source weights instead of
being a weighted mean: in the D1 track's test a 4.2x rescale of the source
weights moved the legacy passive output by 0.16 in relative norm at such
queries. With ρ = 0.02 and interior queries whose median wall distance is
about 5 mm on a 4 m car (below ρ in gauge units) most queries are inside the
kernel's reach, but the far tail of the interior sample is not, so the
legacy passive arm's 2.6x pressure deficit (program book, interior chapter)
includes a contribution from this readout regime that the arm's
measure-scale contract test did not exercise. The legacy path is left
bitwise unchanged so trained checkpoints reproduce; the support path uses an
exactly normalized log-space form (softmax over sources with logits
−d²/ρ² + log w), identical where the mass is not tiny. The PASSIVE-12 arm,
which uses the normalized readout with 12 read blocks and the SDF scalar,
bounds how much of the 2.6x was readout and depth rather than passivity;
the main session has asked for this note to attach a caveat to that figure
once the arm reports.

**Launch acceptance (addendum).** SUPPORT-12 steps at 0.52 s and 10.8 GB
per GPU and SUPPORT-4 at 0.46 s and 7.1 GB (the QT+SDF reference: 0.28 s,
6.3 GB), both at epoch 3–4 within the first hour; the cost readout is
therefore already known to be 1.6–1.9x the reference's step time. The two
PASSIVE-12 chains blocked at model construction: with `support_tokens=false`
the model rejects `query_mass=source_total` (the option needs interacting
query or support tokens), so the override `model.query_mass=geometric_mean`
was added to that arm (inert without interacting tokens), the block markers
were cleared and the chains resubmitted (jobs 691370/691371). The
preregistration is unchanged by this: the arm's definition never involved
a query mass.
